content.text:
I submitted **index 9 (Sb fraction 0.149)** as the best composition, but this campaign didn't find a working photoanode. Every sample I measured gave EQE at noise level, so the "best" pick is only marginally ahead.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.031 | 0.00008 |
| 5 | 0.080 | 0.00009 |
| **9** | **0.149** | **0.00023** |
| 13 | 0.249 | −0.00004 |
| 24 | 0.616 | 0.00006 |

**Why it's all near zero:** the most likely reason is that the 2.1 eV illumination is below the band gap of most phases on this line. The band-gap model (MEGNet) predicts about 3.1 eV for BiSbO₄ and about 2.3 eV for Bi₃SbO₇; Bi₂O₃ is around 2.8 eV. Only the Bi-rich sillenite phase (Bi₁₂SbO₂₀, gap about 1.7 eV) should absorb this light. That phase belongs near index 4–5, but the XRD at index 5 matched Bi₂O₃ and Bi₃SbO₇ instead (similarity 0.72 and 0.66, versus 0.35 for sillenite). So it probably didn't form in the film.

**Coverage gaps:**
- I used all 5 EQE measurements but only 2 of the 5 XRD measurements.
- The Sb 0.30–0.55 region and the far Sb-rich end (above 0.62) were never measured for EQE.
- Index 9 being the top value could be noise rather than a real peak.
